mainTopic: The kinds of אשרה trees, שמואל's ruling on a worshipped tree's new growth, and how to identify an אשרה.
overview: The משנה lists three kinds of אשרה: a tree planted for עבודה זרה is fully forbidden, a tree cut back for עבודה זרה only needs its new growth removed, and a tree with an idol placed under it is permitted once the idol is removed. The גמרא explains that דבי רבי ינאי meant that even bending or grafting the tree does not forbid the whole tree; removing the new growth is enough. שמואל rules that bowing to a tree forbids its later growth. רבי אלעזר challenges him from the משנה, and the גמרא answers that שמואל follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, not the רבנן. רב אשי suggests that maybe everyone forbids the new growth and the argument is only about the trunk. The גמרא shows how the משנה could still fit either side on that reading. A second משנה brings the argument between the חכמים and רבי שמעון over a tree with an idol under it, along with the story in צידן. Finally, רב and שמואל give signs for recognizing a tree of unknown status as an אשרה, and the הלכה follows שמואל.

steps.title: The three kinds of idol-worship trees
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three kinds of אשרה, each with a different law.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three kinds of אשרה. (1) A tree planted from the start for עבודה זרה is forbidden. (2) If someone cut back the tree or trimmed it for עבודה זרה and it regrew, he removes the new growth. (3) If someone placed an idol under the tree and then took it away, the tree is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three cases of trees connected to עבודה זרה and the law for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more the tree itself was made for the idol, the stricter the law. If the tree was planted for the idol, the whole tree is forbidden. If it was cut for the idol, only the new growth is forbidden. If an idol simply stood under it, the tree becomes permitted as soon as the idol is removed.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped or used for עבודה זרה
It regrew, putting out new growth

steps.whatToRemember: Planted for the idol: the whole tree is forbidden. Cut for the idol: remove the new growth. Idol placed underneath: the tree is permitted once the idol is removed.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
There are three kinds of asheira trees:
A tree that one planted from the start

phrases.aramaic: לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הֲרֵי זוֹ אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: for the sake of idol worship is forbidden.
If he cut it back or trimmed it for the sake of idol worship
and it regrew, he removes what regrew.
If he set up an idol beneath it
and then removed it, it is permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree planted for עבודה זרה is forbidden. A tree cut for עבודה זרה only needs its new growth removed. A tree with an idol placed under it is permitted once the idol is removed.

steps.title: דבי רבי ינאי add a condition
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי say the second case of the משנה applies when he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted onto the tree itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: this is when he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted onto the body of the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי attach a condition to the משנה's case of a tree cut for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first we read this as a limit: the new growth is forbidden only if he did something major to the tree, like bending a shoot into the ground or grafting. That is more like replanting than just cutting branches. The next step will test this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, meaning the students, of רבי ינאי
He bent a shoot down and buried it in the ground so it takes root
He grafted a branch onto another tree
The body, meaning the trunk, of the tree itself

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
And this is when he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted
onto the body of the tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי וְהוּא שֶׁהִבְרִיךְ וְהִרְכִּיב בְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל אִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adds a condition to the second case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As first understood, the new growth is forbidden only if he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted onto the tree itself.

steps.title: But the משנה says simple cutting is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges דבי רבי ינאי from the משנה's words 'he cut it back or trimmed it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה, 'he cut it back or trimmed it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the משנה makes the new growth forbidden after simple cutting, with no bending or grafting needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bending or grafting were required, the משנה should have said so. It only says cutting or trimming. So דבי רבי ינאי seem to contradict the משנה's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned! This is used to raise a challenge from a משנה.

phrases.english: But we learned "he cut it back or trimmed it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the reading of דבי רבי ינאי given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only bending or grafting makes the regrowth forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the regrowth forbidden after simple cutting or trimming, so no bigger act can be required.

steps.title: דבי רבי ינאי were talking about removing the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that דבי רבי ינאי were teaching about removing the forbidden status: even after bending or grafting, removing the new growth is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the statement of רבי ינאי's school was said about removing the forbidden status. Even if he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted onto the tree itself, once he removes what regrew, the tree is fine. You might have thought that bending or grafting makes it like a tree planted from the start, so the whole tree should be forbidden. They teach us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves דבי רבי ינאי's statement to a different question. It is not about when the tree becomes forbidden. It is about how the forbidden status goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple cutting already makes the regrowth forbidden, as the משנה says. דבי רבי ינאי add a bigger case: even bending or grafting, which looks like replanting, does not make the whole tree forbidden like the first case of the משנה. Removing the new growth is still enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling, meaning removing the forbidden status
It is fine, it is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Simple cutting makes the new growth forbidden. Even with bending or grafting, the tree is not like one planted for the idol: removing the new growth makes the rest permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: דבי רבי ינאי do not mean that bending or grafting is needed to make the growth forbidden. They mean that even bending or grafting does not forbid the whole tree.

phrases.english: Rather, when the statement of Rabbi Yannai was said,
it was said about removing the forbidden status,
that even though he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted
onto the body of the tree,
when he removes what regrew,
it is fine.
For you might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּהִבְרִיךְ וְהִרְכִּיב בְּגוּפוֹ שֶׁל אִילָן
phrases.english: since he bent a shoot into the ground or grafted onto the body of the tree,
it is like a tree planted from the start,
phrases.notes: This points back to the first case in the משנה, where the whole tree is forbidden.

phrases.english: and the whole tree should be forbidden;
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי לְעִנְיַן בִּיטּוּל אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge by moving the statement to a different question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement is about removing the prohibition, not about creating it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bending or grafting makes it like a tree planted for the idol, so the whole tree would be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after bending or grafting, removing the new growth permits the tree.

steps.title: שמואל: The new growth of a worshipped tree is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if a person bows down to a tree, whatever grows on it afterward is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: If someone bows to a tree, its additional growth is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל: bowing to a tree makes its later growth אסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talked about cutting or trimming a tree for עבודה זרה. שמואל goes further: just bowing to the tree, with no cutting at all, is enough to forbid the new growth. This sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: Shmuel says:
One who bows to a tree,
its additional growth is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is how the printed גמרא has it, and the corrected text uses the word in square brackets instead. Both mean "its added growth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion connected to the משנה's law of a tree cut back for עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bowing to a tree makes its subsequent growth forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר challenges שמואל from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that the משנה forbids new growth only when the tree was cut back or trimmed for עבודה זרה, which suggests bowing alone does not forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר raises an objection: The משנה says, "If he cut it back or trimmed it for idol worship and it regrew, he removes what regrew." So if he cut it back or trimmed it, yes, the new growth is forbidden. If he did not cut it back or trim it, no, it is not forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks שמואל's ruling by reading the משנה carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions cutting or trimming as the cause of the forbidden new growth. That suggests that without cutting, bowing alone does not forbid the new growth. This contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: he cut it back and trimmed it
it regrew, put out new growth
yes / no (the "only this case, not that one" inference)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raises an objection:
If he cut it back or trimmed it for idol worship
and it regrew,
he removes what regrew.
If he cut it back or trimmed it, yes, the growth is forbidden;
if he did not cut it back or trim it, no, it is not!
phrases.notes: He means even if he bowed to the tree. Without cutting, the new growth stays permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that bowing alone forbids the new growth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names cutting or trimming as the condition. That implies no cutting means no prohibition, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows the רבנן, while שמואל follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who forbids a tree that was planted and only later worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could say to you: Whose view is this משנה? It is the רבנן's. And שמואל, who gave his ruling, follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who says: A tree that one planted and later worshipped is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. The משנה and שמואל simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that a tree planted normally and only later worshipped is not forbidden. So for them, only cutting it back for עבודה זרה forbids the new growth. רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that worshipping such a tree does forbid it, so for him bowing alone forbids the new growth, and שמואל follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (an answer on someone's behalf)
he planted it and only later worshipped it

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis',
and Shmuel, who said his ruling,
said it following Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda,
who says: A tree that one planted
and later worshipped is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל הָא מַנִּי רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אלעזר's challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion (the משנה follows one תנא, שמואל follows another).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be the only view, so it seemed to rule out שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the רבנן. שמואל follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who forbids a tree planted and later worshipped, so its new growth is forbidden through bowing alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer depends on the claim that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue about the new growth, and the next step attacks that claim.

steps.title: רב אשי: Maybe the dispute is about the trunk, not the new growth
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי questions the answer. Maybe everyone agrees that new growth is forbidden, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue only about the tree's trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects to this: From where do we know that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן disagree about the added growth? Perhaps the added growth is forbidden according to everyone, and they disagree about its trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges the answer of step 7 by suggesting a different way to understand the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 assumed the two views argue about the new growth. רב אשי says maybe all agree the new growth is forbidden, and the only argument is whether the original trunk is forbidden too. If so, the משנה's רבנן would also forbid new growth from bowing, and the answer for שמואל falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: objects to it, attacks the previous answer

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the new growth is permitted. He is saying it may be forbidden according to everyone, so the argument between the two views must be about something else.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: From where do we know that Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda and the Rabbis
disagree about the added growth?
Perhaps added growth is forbidden according to everyone,
and they disagree about its trunk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 7 that רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן argue about the new growth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The argument could just as easily be about the trunk, with everyone forbidding the new growth. That leaves the answer for שמואל without support.

steps.title: רב אשי shows how each side reads its verse about the trunk
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the alternative argument. רבי יוסי בר יהודה forbids even the trunk, based on "burn their אשרים." The רבנן permit the trunk, based on "cut down their אשרים," which must refer to a tree planted and later worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוסי בר יהודה holds that its trunk is also forbidden, as it is written: "And their אשרים you shall burn in fire." And the רבנן hold that the trunk of the tree is permitted, as it is written: "And their אשרים you shall cut down." Which tree has a cut-off part that is forbidden but a trunk that is permitted? You must say: a tree that one planted and later worshipped!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי backs up his suggestion by showing that each opinion has a פסוק that fits an argument about the trunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning destroys the whole tree, so רבי יוסי בר יהודה learns that even the trunk is forbidden. "Cut down" means removing only part of the tree, so the רבנן learn that only the cut-off growth is forbidden and the trunk is permitted. That fits a tree planted and later worshipped, and it means both sides forbid the new growth.

keyTerms.meaning: their אשרה trees (trees used for idol worship)
you must say, the only possible answer is

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, it is possible that everyone forbids the new growth of a worshipped tree, and the argument between רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן is only about the trunk: "burn" means the whole tree, while "cut down" means only the growth.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda holds:
its trunk is also forbidden,
as it is written: "And their asherim you shall burn in fire,"
and the Rabbis hold: the trunk of the tree is permitted,
as it is written: "And their asherim you shall cut down."
Which is a tree whose cut-off part is forbidden
but its trunk is permitted?
You must say:
a tree that one planted and later worshipped!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה סָבַר עִיקָּרוֹ נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills out רב אשי's challenge from step 8 by showing the פסוקים behind each side of his alternative argument.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's suggestion that the argument is about the trunk, while everyone forbids the new growth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 12:3 ("burn their אשרים") for רבי יוסי בר יהודה, and דברים 7:5 ("cut down their אשרים") for the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this reading is right, the answer given for שמואל in step 7 no longer stands, because even the רבנן would forbid the new growth.

steps.title: Switching the verses to match the earlier discussion
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי heads off an objection. Earlier the גמרא matched the פסוקים the opposite way, so he says to simply reverse which פסוק goes with which opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: earlier we did not explain it this way. Then reverse it. The רבנן's verse goes to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה's verse goes to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי expects someone to say, 'But earlier the גמרא gave the פסוקים the other way around!' He answers: just switch them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an earlier sugya, "burn their אשרים" was the source for the רבנן and "cut down their אשרים" was the source for רבי יוסי בר יהודה. רב אשי's new reading needs the opposite pairing. He says the earlier pairing can simply be flipped, so his reading is not blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
that we did not explain it this way earlier
phrases.notes: Earlier, on 45b, the גמרא matched the two פסוקים to the opposite opinions.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיפוֹךְ רַבָּנַן לִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: reverse: the Rabbis' verse goes to Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda's view,
and Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda's verse goes to the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָא דְּלָא מְתָרְצִינַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אשי's alternative reading by removing a problem raised by the earlier sugya.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier pairing of verses contradicts רב אשי's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse pairing can be flipped, so רב אשי's reading stands.

steps.title: Then whose view is the משנה about cutting back the tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's reading. If everyone forbids new growth, then the משנה that mentions cutting back fits neither the רבנן nor רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, who taught 'he cut it back or trimmed it'? Neither the רבנן nor רבי יוסי בר יהודה! If the רבנן, even without cutting back the new growth is forbidden. If רבי יוסי בר יהודה, even the trunk is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. It says his reading leaves the משנה without anyone it can belong to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב אשי's reading, the רבנן forbid new growth from simply bowing, so the משנה would not need cutting back. רבי יוסי בר יהודה forbids even the trunk, but the משנה forbids only new growth. So the משנה's case matches neither side.

keyTerms.meaning: he cut it back or trimmed it
who teaches it? (whose opinion is it?)
the tree's trunk, the main tree

phrases.english: If so,
'he cut it back or trimmed it' — who teaches it?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבָּנַן וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: Neither the Rabbis nor Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda!
If it is the Rabbis —

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֹא גִּידְּעוֹ וּפִיסְּלוֹ נָמֵי תּוֹסֶפֶת אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: even without cutting it back or trimming it, the new growth is forbidden;
if it is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda —
even the tree's trunk is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן גִּידְּעוֹ וּפִיסְּלוֹ מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading רב אשי just finished defending.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that both sides forbid new growth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's detail of cutting back and its ruling of new growth only cannot fit either side under רב אשי's reading.

steps.title: The משנה can follow רבי יוסי בר יהודה: cutting shows what he wanted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה can fit either side. If it follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה, he forbids the trunk only when the tree was worshipped in a plain way. Cutting back shows the worshipper cares only about the new growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the רבנן; if you want, say רבי יוסי בר יהודה. If רבי יוסי בר יהודה: when he says the trunk is forbidden without cutting back, that is in a plain case. But if he cut it back or trimmed it, he showed that he wants the new growth, not the trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אשי. It says the משנה could belong to either side, and it starts by explaining how it fits רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר יהודה forbids the whole tree only when the person worshipped it in general. Cutting the tree back to make it grow shows he is serving with the new growth, not the trunk. So in the משנה's case only the new growth is forbidden, even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)
in a plain case, with nothing specified
it is what he wants, it suits him

phrases.english: If you want, say it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: and if you want, say it is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: If you want, say it is Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: בְּלֹא גִּידְּעוֹ וּפִיסְּלוֹ עִיקַּר אִילָן אָסוּר
phrases.english: that without cutting it back or trimming it the trunk is forbidden,
that is in a plain case,
phrases.notes: He means the person worshipped the tree in general, without pointing to any specific part.

phrases.english: but if he cut it back or trimmed it —
he has revealed his intention
that the new growth is what he wants,
and the trunk is not what he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by giving the first of two ways to fit the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an opinion (אוקימתא based on the worshipper's intent)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי בר יהודה always forbids the trunk, so the משנה cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: He forbids the trunk only in a plain case. Cutting back shows the worship is aimed at the new growth alone.

steps.title: The משנה can follow the רבנן: it teaches that the trunk stays permitted
steps.stepSummary: The second answer: the משנה follows the רבנן. It mentions cutting back to teach that even an action done to the tree does not forbid the trunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say the רבנן. 'He cut it back or trimmed it' was needed. You might have thought that since he did an action to the tree itself, the trunk should also be forbidden. So it teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second way to fit the משנה: it follows the רבנן. The detail of cutting back is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid new growth even from simply bowing. Still, the משנה needed the cutting case, because one might think that physically working on the tree forbids the trunk too. The משנה teaches that even then only the new growth is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: an action on the thing itself

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers keep רב אשי's reading alive. Under רבי יוסי בר יהודה, cutting back shows the worship is aimed only at the new growth. Under the רבנן, the משנה teaches that even an action on the tree does not forbid the trunk.

phrases.english: Or if you want, say: it is the Rabbis,
and 'he cut it back or trimmed it' was needed.
You might have thought:
since he did an action to the tree itself,
the trunk should also be forbidden,
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבָּנַן גִּידְּעוֹ וּפִיסְּלוֹ אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two answers announced in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: explaining why a seemingly extra detail was needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since he did an action on the tree itself, the trunk should also be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was needed to teach that an action on the tree still does not forbid the trunk.

steps.title: The new משנה: what makes a tree an אשרה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say any tree with an idol under it is an אשרה. רבי שמעון says only a tree that is itself worshipped.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Which tree is an אשרה? Any tree that has an idol beneath it. רבי שמעון says: any tree that people worship.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a basic question: which tree is forbidden as an אשרה? Two opinions are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (the חכמים) says a tree becomes forbidden just because an idol was placed under it. רבי שמעון disagrees: the tree is forbidden only if the tree itself is what people worship.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree connected to idol worship, which is forbidden to benefit from

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole sugya turns on one question: is the tree itself the object of worship, or is it just the place where an idol sits?

phrases.english: MISHNA: Which tree is an אשרה?
Any tree that has an idol beneath it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁעוֹבְדִין אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: any tree that people worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: a tree with an idol under it is an אשרה. רבי שמעון: only a tree that is itself worshipped.

steps.title: The story in צידן: the tree is permitted because they worshipped the image
steps.stepSummary: A worshipped tree had a heap of stones under it. Inside the heap they found an image, so רבי שמעון permitted the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident in צידן with a tree that people worshipped, and they found a heap of stones under it. רבי שמעון told them to examine the heap. They did, and found an image in it. He said: since they worship the image, we will permit the tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story that shows רבי שמעון's view in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first it looked as if the tree itself was being worshipped. Once the hidden image turned up, it was clear the worship was aimed at the image, not the tree. Since רבי שמעון forbids only a tree that is itself worshipped, he permitted the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
An image or figure, here an idol

phrases.english: And there was an incident in Tzaidan
with a tree that people would worship,
and they found a heap of stones beneath it.
Rabbi Shimon said to them:
Examine this heap.
They examined it and found an image in it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: הוֹאִיל וְלַצּוּרָה הֵן עוֹבְדִין,
phrases.english: He said to them: Since it is the image that they worship,
we will permit the tree for them.
phrases.notes: "For them" means for the people who want to use the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי שמעון's opinion from the previous step applied to a real case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's rule that only a tree that is itself worshipped is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident in צידן, where the tree was permitted once the hidden image was found.

steps.title: But the earlier משנה already listed three kinds of אשרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה asks 'which is an אשרה' when the previous משנה already taught three kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: 'Which is an אשרה?' But we already learned that there are three kinds of אשרה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. The question 'which tree is an אשרה' sounds as if we don't already know, but the earlier משנה listed three kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed three trees: one planted for worship, one changed for worship, and one with an idol placed under it. If those were already defined, our משנה's question looks unnecessary or even contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: "Which is an אשרה?"
But we learned "three אשרות"!
phrases.notes: This points back to the previous משנה, which listed three kinds of forbidden trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the opening words of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening question of the משנה, 'איזו אשרה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The previous משנה already defined three kinds of אשרה, so asking 'which one' seems to ignore what we learned.

steps.title: Two kinds are agreed; the משנה asks about the disputed one
steps.stepSummary: Two of the three kinds are forbidden according to everyone. The משנה is asking only about the third kind, which רבי שמעון and the חכמים argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: two kinds are forbidden according to everyone, and one is a dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. Which is the אשרה they disagree about? A tree with an idol under it. רבי שמעון says only a tree that is itself worshipped is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's question. It is not asking about all three kinds, only about the one that is disputed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two trees that are themselves worshipped are forbidden by everyone. The tree with an idol under it is the disputed case: the חכמים forbid it, and רבי שמעון permits it because the tree itself is not worshipped.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not permit every אשרה. He agrees that a tree which is itself worshipped is forbidden. He argues only about a tree that just has an idol under it.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
two are forbidden according to everyone,
and one is a dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.
Which is the אשרה
about which Rabbi Shimon and the Sages disagree?
Any tree that has an idol beneath it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁעוֹבְדִים אוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: for Rabbi Shimon says: only a tree that people worship is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the question refers only to the disputed case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be redefining אשרה from scratch, ignoring the three kinds already taught.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is asking only about the third kind, the tree with an idol under it, which רבי שמעון and the חכמים argue about.

steps.title: How do we recognize an אשרה when nobody saw it worshipped?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a tree count as an אשרה when we have no clear information about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which tree counts as a plain אשרה, without our knowing for sure that it was worshipped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new practical question and sets up the answers of רב and שמואל that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed trees whose status we know. Now the question is which signs let us treat a tree as an אשרה when nobody actually saw it being worshipped.

phrases.english: Which tree is a plain אשרה?
phrases.notes: "Plain" here means we never saw it worshipped, so we must judge by signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute in the משנה to a practical question about identifying an אשרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What signs show that a tree of unknown status is an אשרה.

steps.title: רב: the priests sit under it and won't eat its fruit
steps.stepSummary: רב says that if idol priests sit under a tree and refuse to eat its fruit, it is an אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: any tree that idol priests sit under and whose fruit they do not taste.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer to the question: a sign that the priests treat the tree as holy to their idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting under the tree on its own would not prove much. The fact that the priests will not eat its fruit shows they treat the fruit as belonging to the idol, so the tree is an אשרה.

phrases.english: Rav said:
any tree that idol priests sit beneath
and do not taste from its fruits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כֹּל שֶׁכּוֹמָרִים יוֹשְׁבִין תַּחְתֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tree is an אשרה if the priests sit under it and refuse to eat its fruit.

steps.title: שמואל: even saying the dates are for the idol-house is enough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that even if they only say the dates are for the house of נצרפי, the tree is forbidden, because they use the dates in a drink for their festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: even if they say, "these dates are for the house of נצרפי," the tree is forbidden, because they throw the dates into beer and drink it on their festival day.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second, wider answer. A tree can count as an אשרה even when its fruit is eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, refusing to eat the fruit is the sign. For שמואל, even setting the fruit aside for use in the idol's festival makes the tree an אשרה, although people do drink the beer made from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of נצרפי, a house of idol worship

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
even if they say, "These dates are for the house of Natzrefei,"
it is forbidden,
because they throw them into beer
and drink it on their festival day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader answer than רב to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even setting the dates aside for the idol's festival drink makes the tree an אשרה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אמימר reports from the elders of פומבדיתא that the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: the elders of פומבדיתא told me that the הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר settles the argument between רב and שמואל in favor of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical ruling follows the broader view. A tree whose dates are set aside for the idol's festival drink is forbidden, even if nobody refuses to eat its fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה, the final ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים forbid a tree with an idol under it, while רבי שמעון forbids only a tree that is itself worshipped. For a tree of unknown status, the הלכה follows שמואל: even setting its fruit aside for the idol's festival makes it an אשרה.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
the elders of Pumbedita told me
the halacha follows Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר אֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב (step 19) and שמואל (step 20).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל: setting the dates aside for the idol-house is enough to make the tree an אשרה.
